records.claim: Some, but not all, studies have suggested that when people take SSRIs such as citalopram or escitalopram during the second half of pregnancy, their babies might have a higher chance of a serious lung condition called persistent pulmonary hypertension (PPH). In the general population, PPH happens in 1 or 2 out of every 1,000 births. Some studies suggest that the overall chance of PPH when an SSRI is used in pregnancy is less than 1 out of every 100 births (less than 1%).
records.source_section: Does taking citalopram or escitalopram in pregnancy increase the chance of other pregnancy-related problems?
